title: High-speed infrared thermal measurements of impacted metallic solids
author: Nieto-Fuentes, Osovski, et al.

steps.title: Remove calibration components
steps.instruction: After completing thermal calibration, remove the soldering iron and the dummy specimen from the setup, and discontinue use of the optical chopper.

steps.title: Acquire and synchronize signals
steps.instruction: Record the incident strain‑gage, transmitter strain‑gage, and infrared temperature‑rise signals; shift the elastic‑wave signals according to the distances between the strain gages and the specimen and the known wave velocity so that they align with the thermal signal.

substeps.instruction: Identify the time when the stress wave reaches the incident strain gage (t1 = 87 µs).
Add the travel time from the incident strain gage to the specimen plus the elastic deformation time to obtain t2 = 213 µs.
Select the portion of the IR temperature signal that corresponds to plastic deformation up to t3 = 314 µs.
Note that the specimen is a pure nickel deformed at a strain rate of 4690 s⁻¹.

steps.title: Verify synchronization
steps.instruction: Plot stress versus plastic strain together with the temperature profile; confirm that the temperature rise begins at approximately zero plastic strain and continues to specimen failure, and ensure only the first impact is considered.

description: Recent works where the previous methodology was successfully proven can be found in [17,18].
